paper_metadata.title: Discovery of a Ni-based superalloy with low thermal expansion via machine learning

evidence.quote: Traditional Ni-based superalloys are widely used due to their excellent high-temperature performance; however, their high thermal expansion at elevated temperatures limits their further application in the modern aerospace industry.
Alloy 3 with the lowest CTE (11.26 e-6 ◦C-1) exhibits a substantial 14.7 % reduction, which is observed in the uncommon Ni-Mo-W system.

machine_learning_models.name: support vector regression (SVR)
machine_learning_models.task: prediction of coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of Ni-based superalloys
machine_learning_models.dataset: 137 alloys and 1159 CTE data points from Superalloys Handbook, MatWeb and CINDAS; train 85% (981 points), test 15% (178 points)
machine_learning_models.validation: 5-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter optimization; evaluation on held-out test set

evidence.quote: the Support Vector Regression (SVR) model exhibits outstanding robustness in the datasets (R2_train = 0.822, MSE_train = 0.611, R2_test = 0.844, MSE_test = 0.401) after feature engineering.
